base_method_text.title: Diffusion Model-Augmented Behavioral Cloning
base_method_text.summary:
Imitation learning addresses the challenge of learning by observing an
expert's demonstrations without access to reward signals from environments.
Most existing imitation learning methods that do not require interacting with
environments either model the expert distribution as the conditional
probability p(a|s) (e.g., behavioral cloning, BC) or the joint probability p(s,
a). Despite the simplicity of modeling the conditional probability with BC, it
usually struggles with generalization. While modeling the joint probability can
improve generalization performance, the inference procedure is often
time-consuming, and the model can suffer from manifold overfitting. This work
proposes an imitation learning framework that benefits from modeling both the
conditional and joint probability of the expert distribution. Our proposed
Diffusion Model-Augmented Behavioral Cloning (DBC) employs a diffusion model
trained to model expert behaviors and learns a policy to optimize both the BC
loss (conditional) and our proposed diffusion model loss (joint). DBC
outperforms baselines in various continuous control tasks in navigation, robot
arm manipulation, dexterous manipulation, and locomotion. We design additional
experiments to verify the limitations of modeling either the conditional
probability or the joint probability of the expert distribution, as well as
compare different generative models. Ablation studies justify the effectiveness
of our design choices.
base_method_text.main_contributions: The paper introduces Diffusion Model-Augmented Behavioral Cloning (DBC), a novel imitation learning framework that combines the strengths of modeling both the conditional probability p(a|s) (Behavioral Cloning) and the joint probability p(s, a) (Diffusion Models) of expert demonstrations. DBC outperforms baselines in various continuous control tasks.
base_method_text.methodology: DBC uses a diffusion model to capture the joint probability of expert state-action pairs and trains a policy to optimize both the standard behavioral cloning loss (conditional probability) and a diffusion model loss (joint probability). The diffusion model loss guides the policy towards actions that align with the expert distribution.
base_method_text.experimental_setup: The framework was evaluated on continuous control tasks including navigation (MAZE), robot arm manipulation (FETCH PICK), dexterous manipulation (HAND ROTATE), and locomotion (CHEETAH, WALKER, ANTREACH). The performance was compared against Behavioral Cloning (BC), Implicit BC (IBC), and Diffusion Policy, using success rate and return as metrics. Generalization was tested by injecting noise into initial states and goal locations.
base_method_text.limitations: The framework is designed to learn from expert trajectories without environment interactions and cannot directly learn from agent trajectories. The method inherits biases from the expert demonstrators.
base_method_text.future_research_directions: Future research could extend the method to incorporate agent data, potentially allowing for improvement when interacting with environments is possible. Addressing biases inherited from expert demonstrators is another area for future work.

add_method_texts.title: FiT: Flexible Vision Transformer for Diffusion Model
add_method_texts.summary:
Nature is infinitely resolution-free. In the context of this reality,
existing diffusion models, such as Diffusion Transformers, often face
challenges when processing image resolutions outside of their trained domain.
To overcome this limitation, we present the Flexible Vision Transformer (FiT),
a transformer architecture specifically designed for generating images with
unrestricted resolutions and aspect ratios. Unlike traditional methods that
perceive images as static-resolution grids, FiT conceptualizes images as
sequences of dynamically-sized tokens. This perspective enables a flexible
training strategy that effortlessly adapts to diverse aspect ratios during both
training and inference phases, thus promoting resolution generalization and
eliminating biases induced by image cropping. Enhanced by a meticulously
adjusted network structure and the integration of training-free extrapolation
techniques, FiT exhibits remarkable flexibility in resolution extrapolation
generation. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the exceptional performance
of FiT across a broad range of resolutions, showcasing its effectiveness both
within and beyond its training resolution distribution. Repository available at
https://github.com/whlzy/FiT.
add_method_texts.main_contributions: The paper introduces Flexible Vision Transformer (FiT), a novel transformer architecture for diffusion models, enabling image generation at arbitrary resolutions and aspect ratios. Key contributions include a flexible training pipeline eliminating cropping, a dynamic token length modeling architecture, and a training-free resolution extrapolation method, achieving state-of-the-art performance across various resolutions.
add_method_texts.methodology: FiT models images as sequences of dynamically-sized tokens, using a flexible training pipeline that maintains aspect ratios and resizes images to fit a maximum token limit. The architecture incorporates 2D Rotary Positional Embedding (RoPE), Swish-Gated Linear Unit (SwiGLU), and Masked Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA). Training-free extrapolation techniques like VisionNTK and VisionYaRN are adapted for resolution generalization.
add_method_texts.experimental_setup: The model was trained on the ImageNet dataset with a maximum token length of 256. Performance was evaluated using Fre'chet Inception Distance (FID), sFID, Inception Score (IS), Precision, and Recall. Experiments were conducted on in-distribution (256x256, 160x320, 128x384) and out-of-distribution (320x320, 224x448, 160x480) resolutions, comparing FiT against state-of-the-art CNN and transformer-based generative models.
add_method_texts.limitations: The FiT-XL/2 model was trained for a limited number of steps (1.8M), resulting in slightly inferior performance compared to DiT-XL/2 at the training resolution (256x256). The generative capabilities of FiT-XL/2 were not fully explored with higher resolution training. Furthermore, the research primarily focused on training-free resolution extrapolation techniques, without exploring methods requiring additional training.
add_method_texts.future_research_directions: Future research directions include exploring the generative capabilities of FiT with higher resolution training, investigating resolution extrapolation methods that require additional training, and further studies on generating images with arbitrary resolutions and aspect ratios, enabled by the flexibility of FiT.

base_experimental_code: The repository implements A2C, PPO, and ACKTR algorithms. There is no explicit implementation of Diffusion Model-Augmented Behavioral Cloning (DBC). However, 'a2c_ppo_acktr/algo/gail.py' shows the implementation of Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning (GAIL).
base_experimental_info: The repository provides a framework for implementing reinforcement learning algorithms, including A2C, PPO, and ACKTR. It includes tools for creating environments, defining policies, and training agents. The 'arguments.py' file specifies various hyperparameters for training, such as learning rate, entropy coefficient, value loss coefficient, and maximum gradient norm. The 'envs.py' file handles environment creation and preprocessing, including support for Atari environments. The 'gail.py' file implements GAIL, which is an imitation learning technique. While the repository doesn't directly implement DBC, the GAIL implementation could potentially be adapted to incorporate diffusion models.
